availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl
availableCommands.description: Search, scrape, and interact with the web via the Firecrawl CLI. Use this skill whenever the user wants to search the web, find articles, research a topic, look something up online, scrape a webpage, grab content from a URL, get data from a website, crawl documentation, download a site, or interact with pages that need clicks or logins. Also use when they say "fetch this page", "pull the content from", "get the page at https://", or reference external websites. This provides real-time web search with full page content and interact capabilities — beyond what Claude can do natively with built-in tools. Do NOT trigger for local file operations, git commands, deployments, or code editing tasks.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-agent
availableCommands.description: AI-powered autonomous data extraction that navigates complex sites and returns structured JSON. Use this skill when the user wants structured data from websites, needs to extract pricing tiers, product listings, directory entries, or any data as JSON with a schema. Triggers on "extract structured data", "get all the products", "pull pricing info", "extract as JSON", or when the user provides a JSON schema for website data. More powerful than simple scraping for multi-page structured extraction.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-build-interact

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-build-onboarding
availableCommands.description: Get Firecrawl credentials and SDK setup into a project. This skill includes its own browser auth flow, so it does not depend on the website onboarding skill.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-build-scrape
availableCommands.description: Integrate Firecrawl `/scrape` into product code for single-page extraction. Use when an app already has a URL and needs markdown, HTML, links, screenshots, metadata, or structured page output. Prefer this skill over broader crawl patterns when the feature is page-level.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-build-search

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-company-directories

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-competitive-intel
availableCommands.description: Monitor competitor pricing, features, changelogs, dashboards, and product changes with Firecrawl. Use for recurring competitive intelligence, pricing tier extraction, feature change tracking, or structured competitor alerts.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-crawl
availableCommands.description: Bulk extract content from an entire website or site section. Use this skill when the user wants to crawl a site, extract all pages from a docs section, bulk-scrape multiple pages following links, or says "crawl", "get all the pages", "extract everything under /docs", "bulk extract", or needs content from many pages on the same site. Handles depth limits, path filtering, and concurrent extraction.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-dashboard-reporting

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-deep-research

Use only when the user needs rigorous synthesis of a complex topic (scientific, technical, policy, or market-analytical) that cannot be answered with a short search, and wants a formal written report, not a recommendation list. availableCommands.name: firecrawl-demo-walkthrough
availableCommands.description: Walk through a product's key flows with Firecrawl browser and produce a structured UX/product walkthrough. Use for signup, onboarding, pricing, docs, dashboard, product demo prep, UX teardown, and first-run experience analysis.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-download
availableCommands.description: Download an entire website as local files — markdown, screenshots, or multiple formats per page. Use this skill when the user wants to save a site locally, download documentation for offline use, bulk-save pages as files, or says "download the site", "save as local files", "offline copy", "download all the docs", or "save for reference". Combines site mapping and scraping into organized local directories.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-interact
availableCommands.description: Control and interact with a live browser session on any scraped page — click buttons, fill forms, navigate flows, and extract data using natural language prompts or code. Use when the user needs to interact with a webpage beyond simple scraping: logging into a site, submitting forms, clicking through pagination, handling infinite scroll, navigating multi-step checkout or wizard flows, or when a regular scrape failed because content is behind JavaScript interaction. Also useful for authenticated scraping via profiles. Triggers on "interact", "click", "fill out the form", "log in to", "sign in", "submit", "paginated", "next page", "infinite scroll", "interact with the page", "navigate to", "open a session", or "scrape failed".

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-knowledge-base
availableCommands.description: Build a knowledge base from web content with Firecrawl. Use for local reference docs, RAG-ready chunks, fine-tuning datasets, documentation mirrors, topic corpora, or LLM-ready markdown organized from web sources.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-knowledge-ingest
availableCommands.description: Ingest public or authenticated knowledge bases and docs portals with Firecrawl browser. Use for JS-heavy docs, login-gated portals, paginated help centers, support knowledge bases, or structured JSON/markdown extraction from documentation sites.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-lead-gen
availableCommands.description: Generate structured lead lists from prospect databases and web directories with Firecrawl browser. Use for finding prospects by role, company type, industry, stage, location, technologies, or other criteria and exporting CRM-ready JSON or CSV.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-lead-research
availableCommands.description: Produce pre-meeting lead intelligence briefs with Firecrawl. Use when the user needs company research, person research, recent news, talking points, pain points, or outreach preparation before a sales call, partnership meeting, investor conversation, or customer interview.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-map
availableCommands.description: Discover and list all URLs on a website, with optional search filtering. Use this skill when the user wants to find a specific page on a large site, list all URLs, see the site structure, find where something is on a domain, or says "map the site", "find the URL for", "what pages are on", or "list all pages". Essential when the user knows which site but not which exact page.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-market-research
availableCommands.description: Extract market, financial, earnings, industry, and company metrics with Firecrawl. Use when the user asks for market research, industry trends, public company data, financial comparisons, earnings research, or structured market reports.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-parse
availableCommands.description: Efficiently extract and convert the contents of any local file—such as PDF, DOCX, DOC, ODT, RTF, XLSX, XLS, or HTML—into clean, well-formatted markdown saved to disk. Use this skill whenever the user requests to parse, read, or extract information from a file on their computer, including phrases like “parse this PDF”, “convert this document”, “read this file”, “extract text from”, or when a local file path (not a URL) is provided. This skill offers advanced options like generating AI-powered summaries and answering questions based on the file's content. Prefer this tool over `scrape` when handling local files to deliver precise, structured outputs for downstream tasks.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-qa
availableCommands.description: QA test a live website with Firecrawl browser and scrape evidence. Use when the user wants exploratory QA, form testing, navigation/link checks, responsive checks, performance observations, bug reports, or a pre-launch quality review.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-research-index
availableCommands.description: Find the papers that answer a research query with Firecrawl Research, using semantic search, semantic and structural expansion, and in-body verification. Always use this skill for any literature-finding / paper-retrieval task — single-paper lookups or full multi-paper sets.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-research-papers
availableCommands.description: Find and synthesize research papers, whitepapers, PDFs, technical reports, and academic sources with Firecrawl Research, using semantic paper search, related-paper expansion, and in-body verification. Use when the user wants a literature review, paper summary, research landscape, or sourced synthesis from PDFs and scholarly/industry publications.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-scrape
availableCommands.description: Extract clean markdown from any URL, including JavaScript-rendered SPAs. Use this skill whenever the user provides a URL and wants its content, says "scrape", "grab", "fetch", "pull", "get the page", "extract from this URL", or "read this webpage". Handles JS-rendered pages, multiple concurrent URLs, and returns LLM-optimized markdown. Use this instead of WebFetch for any webpage content extraction.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-search
availableCommands.description: Web search with full page content extraction. Use this skill whenever the user asks to search the web, find articles, research a topic, look something up, find recent news, discover sources, or says "search for", "find me", "look up", "what are people saying about", or "find articles about". Returns real search results with optional full-page markdown — not just snippets. Provides capabilities beyond Claude's built-in WebSearch.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-seo-audit
availableCommands.description: Audit a website's SEO with Firecrawl. Use when the user asks for an SEO audit, metadata and heading review, sitemap/site-structure analysis, keyword opportunities, competitor SERP comparison, or prioritized search optimization recommendations.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-shop
availableCommands.description: Research products across the web with Firecrawl and produce a shopping recommendation or cart-ready summary. Use when the user wants to compare products, find the best option, evaluate reviews, respect budget/preferences, or shop with a saved browser session.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-website-design-clone
availableCommands.description: Extract any website's design system into an agent-ready DESIGN.md using Firecrawl scrape evidence. Use when the user wants colors, fonts, spacing, components, layout patterns, or brand/UI guidance from a website so AI agents can create new websites, clone a look, or build pages inspired by that design.

availableCommands.name: firecrawl-workflows
availableCommands.description: Run outcome-focused Firecrawl workflows that produce deliverables such as research reports, SEO audits, QA reports, lead lists, knowledge bases, website design systems, and other structured web-data artifacts. Use when the user wants Firecrawl to complete a business, marketing, product, or creative workflow rather than merely scrape a page or integrate API calls into code.

rawInput.text:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

This document specifies the small-order surcharge feature for the pricing library. Orders with a subtotal below $20.00 will incur a $2.00 surcharge to cover handling costs for small orders. This feature consists of a standalone rule function and a cart method that applies the rule while handling the empty-cart edge case.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1

**User Story:** As a pricing system, I need to calculate the small-order surcharge based on a given subtotal so that orders below the minimum threshold incur the appropriate fee.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the subtotal is below 20.00 (for example 5.00) THEN the system SHALL return 2.00 as the surcharge.

2. WHEN the subtotal is 20.00 or more (for example 20.00 and 35.00) THEN the system SHALL return 0.00 as the surcharge.

3. WHEN the subtotal is 19.99 (just below the threshold) THEN the system SHALL return 2.00 as the surcharge.

### Requirement 2

**User Story:** As a shopping cart, I need to compute my own small-order surcharge by applying the rule to my subtotal so that the surcharge can be included in order totals.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the cart is non-empty and its subtotal is below 20.00 THEN the system SHALL return 2.00 as the surcharge, and WHEN the cart is non-empty and its subtotal is 20.00 or more THEN the system SHALL return 0.00 as the surcharge.

2. WHEN the cart is empty THEN the system SHALL return 0.00 as the surcharge.

# Requirements Document

## Introduction

This document specifies the small-order surcharge feature for the pricing library. Orders with a subtotal below $20.00 will incur a $2.00 surcharge to cover handling costs for small orders. This feature consists of a standalone rule function and a cart method that applies the rule while handling the empty-cart edge case.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1

**User Story:** As a pricing system, I need to calculate the small-order surcharge based on a given subtotal so that orders below the minimum threshold incur the appropriate fee.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the subtotal is below 20.00 (for example 5.00) THEN the system SHALL return 2.00 as the surcharge.

2. WHEN the subtotal is 20.00 or more (for example 20.00 and 35.00) THEN the system SHALL return 0.00 as the surcharge.

3. WHEN the subtotal is 19.99 (just below the threshold) THEN the system SHALL return 2.00 as the surcharge.

### Requirement 2

**User Story:** As a shopping cart, I need to compute my own small-order surcharge by applying the rule to my subtotal so that the surcharge can be included in order totals.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the cart is non-empty and its subtotal is below 20.00 THEN the system SHALL return 2.00 as the surcharge, and WHEN the cart is non-empty and its subtotal is 20.00 or more THEN the system SHALL return 0.00 as the surcharge.

2. WHEN the cart is empty THEN the system SHALL return 0.00 as the surcharge.

# Design Document

## Overview

The small-order surcharge feature adds a $2.00 handling fee to orders with subtotals below $20.00. The design separates the pure pricing rule from cart-specific logic, enabling reuse and simplifying testing.

## Architecture

The feature consists of two components:

1. **Rule Module** (`src/pricing/surcharge.py`): A standalone module containing the threshold-based surcharge calculation
2. **Cart Method** (`Cart.small_order_surcharge()`): A cart-aware method that applies the rule with empty-cart handling

This separation follows the existing pattern in the pricing library where pure calculation functions exist independently of domain objects.

## Components and Interfaces

### `src/pricing/surcharge.py`

**Function:** `small_order_surcharge(subtotal: Decimal) -> Decimal`

- **Input:** `subtotal` - A `Decimal` representing the order subtotal with two decimal places
- **Output:** A `Decimal` with two decimal places representing the surcharge amount (2.00 or 0.00)
- **Logic:** Returns `Decimal("2.00")` if `subtotal < Decimal("20.00")`, otherwise returns `Decimal("0.00")`

### `Cart.small_order_surcharge()`

**Method:** `Cart.small_order_surcharge(self) -> Decimal`

- **Input:** Implicit (operates on the cart's own state)
- **Output:** A `Decimal` with two decimal places representing the surcharge amount
- **Logic:** 
  - If the cart is empty, returns `Decimal("0.00")` directly
  - Otherwise, calls `small_order_surcharge(self.subtotal())` and returns the result

## Data Models

All monetary values are represented as `Decimal` objects with two decimal places, consistent with the existing `Cart` and `LineItem` implementation.

**Constants:**
- Threshold: `Decimal("20.00")`
- Surcharge amount: `Decimal("2.00")`
- No surcharge: `Decimal("0.00")`

**Cart state determination:**
- A cart is considered empty when it contains no line items (length check or equivalent)

## Error Handling

No special error handling is required. The function assumes valid `Decimal` inputs. Invalid inputs (negative subtotals, None values) are outside the scope of this feature and should be prevented by the calling code or handled by existing cart validation.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests for Rule Module

Test `small_order_surcharge()` with:
- Subtotal below threshold (e.g., 5.00) → expects 2.00
- Subtotal at threshold (20.00) → expects 0.00
- Subtotal above threshold (e.g., 35.00) → expects 0.00
- Subtotal just below threshold (19.99) → expects 2.00

### Unit Tests for Cart Method

Test `Cart.small_order_surcharge()` with:
- Non-empty cart with subtotal below 20.00 → expects 2.00
- Non-empty cart with subtotal at or above 20.00 → expects 0.00
- Empty cart → expects 0.00

### Property Tests (Optional)

Property-based tests can verify that:
- For all subtotals in [0, 19.99], surcharge equals 2.00
- For all subtotals >= 20.00, surcharge equals 0.00
- Surcharge is always non-negative
- Surcharge is always either 0.00 or 2.00 (no intermediate values)

## Correctness Properties

1. **Threshold Correctness:** The surcharge transitions from 2.00 to 0.00 exactly at the 20.00 boundary
2. **Monotonicity:** As subtotal increases, surcharge never increases (non-increasing function)
3. **Empty Cart Safety:** An empty cart never incurs a surcharge regardless of the rule's output
4. **Precision:** All monetary calculations preserve two decimal places
5. **Idempotency:** Multiple calls with the same subtotal always return the same surcharge
